messages:
maya: heads-up: LCP on /dashboard jumped from 1.1s -> 3.8s in prod canary at 09:15. charts (metric cartogram + heatmap) noticeably slow. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy finished: deploy/2026-03-18T09:12Z by priscilla. image: inference-console:v6.2.3

sanjay: saw the spike in SLO graphs, correlated with bundle size delta. webpack stats: \"main\" +340KB gzip. could be new telemetry import.

devon: +1, telemetry sdk v2 pulled in an intl polyfill and full analytics client. stacktrace shows parse/compile on main thread.

maya: quick paste of build log:
```
asset: main.js 12.4 MB
 + 352.1 kB  vendor/telemetry-client.js
```

leo: Is prefetching/bundles changed in the rollout? routing/prefetch policy was tightened this morning.

ashley: yes, prefetch policy moved to aggressive for canary: PREFETCH: routes=[\"/dashboard\",\"/workspace/*\"] concurrency=3

sanjay: that will warm KV cache but also cause many bundles to be parsed on initial navigation. combo with telemetry import = bad.

devon: quick check: disabling telemetry import locally removes vendor/telemetry-client.js and LCP drops ~1.2s. can we hotfix by lazy-loading telemetry?

maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/4982 adds dynamic import for telemetry + guard when low-end devices detected. canary not rolled yet.

deploy-bot: New rollback request created #INC-5567

ops-bot: Rolling back canary to inference-console:v6.2.2 in us-east-1 only. ETA 5m.

priscilla: If rollback accepted, we should also throttle prefetch concurrency and revert aggressive route list. I'll make quick patch.

leo: also check telemetry sampling config — it enabled full-fidelity on canary which triggers heavy telemetry boot. samplingDelta=1.0 in canary config.

maya: action items: 1) rollback canary (ops) 2) revert prefetch change (priscilla) 3) merge lazy-load telemetry PR (devon) 4) follow-up to split intl polyfill (sanjay). I'll create follow-up ticket and assign.

maya: created ticket PLAT-7894 and linked PRs.

devon: once rollback done I'll run a small A/B canary that disables prefetch but keeps other changes to isolate.

sanjay: FYI tagging @eng-sre to monitor LCP and frontend error budget.

eng-sre: on it, we'll watch synthetic and real-user LCP and report back in 10m. :mag:

maya: thanks — keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
